question: Should OpenClaw expose a file-based internal `session:end` hook event, or should workflow orchestration use the existing typed plugin `session_end` lifecycle hook instead?
rationale: Both surfaces are plausible, but VISION.md favors lean core and plugin-owned optional capability while the internal hooks docs position `HOOK.md` scripts as small operator automation; choosing the permanent contract is maintainer product/API intent, not an automatic repair decision.

options.title: Document plugin boundary
options.body: Treat typed plugin `session_end` as the supported orchestration hook, update internal hook docs to say so, and then close this request once the docs are clear.

options.title: Add internal event
options.body: Implement a real internal `session:end` event and guard, wire reset/delete/shutdown/subagent/cron completion paths, and add focused hook/docs tests.

options.title: Keep linked PR scoped
options.body: Review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/61675 only as daily/idle reset-memory work and keep this broader internal-event request separate.

recommendation.title: Document plugin boundary
recommendation.body: Treat typed plugin `session_end` as the supported orchestration hook, update internal hook docs to say so, and then close this request once the docs are clear.

likelyOwner.reason: The available hook/plugin history and issue timeline point to Vincent as the best current routing candidate for this hook API boundary.
